title: Quantitative 3D analysis and visualization of cardiac fibrosis by microcomputed tomography
protocol: Harvest hearts at 28 days post-MI as described in Janbandhu et al. (2021).
Transfer each heart to a 15 mL falcon tube filled with fixative solution and place the tube on a rocker at 4°C for 1 day.
Remove the fixative and fill the tube with hydrogel solution, then continue rocking at 4°C for 3 days.
Immerse the heart in hydrogel in a 12-well tissue culture plate.
Place the plate in the X-Clarity Polymerization System without the lid.
Initiate polymerization using the following settings: Pressure: −90 kPa; temperature: 37°C; time: 3 h.
Separate hearts from the encasing gel and remove any extraneous gel carefully.
Rinse hearts in 1× PBS.
Keep hearts in PBS for at least 10–15 minutes to ensure complete removal of hydrogel pieces and PFA traces.
Place hearts in a 15 mL falcon tube containing 15 mL of Lugol’s solution.
Wrap the tube with aluminum foil to exclude light.
Place the tube on a rocker at room temperature for 3 days to ensure penetration of iodine throughout the hydrogel mesh.
Replace Lugol’s solution after 2 days.
Remove the heart from the staining solution and place on lint-free tissue paper to remove excess liquid.
Place the heart in a 1.5 mL tube in a vertical position.
Gently tap the tube 3-4 times to ensure the heart has settled at the bottom of the tube.
Seal the tube with parafilm to keep the sample moist during scanning.
Fix the tube on the sample holder using dental wax.
Load the samples mounted on the specimen holder in the sample changer so that the heart is positioned directly over the axis of rotation.
Position the heart to rotate around the central apical-basal axis when the mount is rotated.
Load the sample correctly to avoid movement during scanning.
Ensure the sample is properly secured and does not dry out.
Start SkyScan1272 software to open the main screen with control elements.
Click on the “X-ray” icon in the toolbar menu to switch on X-ray.
Wait for the X-ray warm-up which generally takes ∼15–30 minutes.
After X-ray warm-up, click on the “X-ray” icon again to switch off X-ray.
Insert the sample inside the specimen chamber using the “Sample changer” control panel.
Click on the “Insert” button in the “Sample changer” control panel to insert the first sample into the chamber.
Once the robotic arm returns to its starting position, click on the “Door” icon to close the specimen chamber.
Do not click on the “Door” icon to close the specimen chamber until the robotic arm returns to a complete rest at the starting position.
Position the sample in the center of the field of view by clicking on the “X-ray” and “Grab” icon in the toolbar menu.
Visualize the X-ray image in the display window continuously.
Move the sample in a vertical direction by pressing the “Ctrl” button and left mouse button simultaneously, dragging the mouse pointer in the desired direction.
Alternatively, use arrows in the status bar to position the sample in the center of the field of view.
Adjust the filter, resolution, voltage, and pixel size for optimal transmission of the X-ray.
Activate the profile line by right clicking on the sample image in the display window.
Assess transmission values which should be between 10 and 50% (30% is ideal).
Select resolution: 2452 × 1640 pixels.
Use slider to achieve 5 μm pixel size.
Select the filter: 0.5 mm aluminium + Cu 0.038 and note down camera position (e.g., close).
Note down the vertical position of the sample for each individual sample.
Rotate the sample using the slider and ensure it is not out of field of view during rotation.
Perform flat-field correction.
Remove the sample from the specimen chamber by clicking the “Remove” button on the “Sample changer” control panel.
Close the door by clicking on the “Door” icon from the main toolbar menu.
Click on the “X-ray” and “Grab” icons on the toolbar menu.
Enter the exact values of all parameters set for the sample at step 9 in the status bar.
Ensure the field of view is completely empty and the background is homogeneous.
Switch off flat-field correction by double-clicking on “ff” displayed at the upper left corner of the screen.
Click the right mouse button in the imaging area to show a signal intensity profile along the line where the mouse pointer is situated.
Remove the profile from the image by clicking the right mouse button again.
Display the “Scanning modes” window by clicking on “Option” > “Scanning modes” from the main menu.
Make the “Scanning modes” option accessible by pressing Ctrl + Alt + Shift + S if it is greyed out.
Adjust the exposure time in the correct box (2452 × 1640) in the “Exposure (ms) for camera position close to the source” panel.
Tick the box next to “Do not update flat-field references.”
Click on the “OK” button after adjusting the exposure time.
Check the signal intensity value; if it is not around 60%, repeat steps 10f–g.
Open the “Scanning modes” window and tick the box next to “Update flat-fields for marked modes and modes with modified exposure.”
Click on the “OK” button to apply the new flat-field configuration.
Double click on “flat-field correction OFF” to switch on flat-field correction.
Click on the “X-ray” icon in the toolbar menu to turn off X-ray.
Proceed to acquisition.
If any of the acquisition parameters are changed, perform flat-field corrections using the revised setting.
If the exposure is changed, perform dark field flat-field correction with X-ray turned off.
Tick the box next to “Update flat-fields for marked modes and modes with modified exposure” in the “Scanning modes” window.
Untick the box next to “Update only bright flat-field reference”.
Click on the “OK” button.
Re-insert the sample and proceed further.
Select the “Manual” option under “Protocol” in the “Sample changer” control panel.
Enter a “Filename prefix” for the sample.
Click on “browse” button to select a destination folder for data directory.
Set rotation step (deg) to 0.4.
Do not tick the box next to “Averaging (frames)”.
Do not tick the box next to “Random movement (pix)”.
Tick the box next to “360 deg scanning”.
Select filter determined in step 9c for Energy filter.
Select pixel size (μm) value determined in step 9b.
Select image format value determined in step 9a.
Type the vertical position value determined for this sample in step 9e.
Set partial width to 100%.
Validate setting by rotating the sample 0/90/180 degrees to ensure it stays within boundary.
Tick the box next to “standard scan in central camera position”.
Do not tick the box next to “Oversize scan”.
Click on the “OK” button.
Select "Open data" icon in NRecon toolbar menu.
Adjust reconstruction parameters manually, including misalignment compensation, ring artifacts reduction, smoothing and beam hardening correction for optimum image quality.
Click on “Start scanning” button in the “Sample changer” control panel after entering values of acquisition parameters for each sample.
Browse and select 1 file from the selected folder and click “Open” to load the data.
Display the scanned image in the display window.
Open the “Reconstruction” window on the right side of the screen.
If the “Reconstruction” window is not displayed automatically, visualize it from the “View” option in the main menu.
Select the “Setting” tab in the “Reconstruction” window.
Tick the box next to “Smoothing” and use an initial value of “1”.
Tick the box next to “Misalignment compensation” and use the default value.
Tick the box next to “Ring artifacts reduction” and use an initial value of “1”.
Tick the box next to “Beam-hardening correction” and set it to an initial value of 10%.
Select the “Start” tab in the “Reconstruction” window.
Move the outer 2 red lines closer to the heart image to crop as much empty space as possible.
Keep the middle green line in the center of the heart image.
Select “Fine tuning” in the “Start” tab to adjust/improve the above-mentioned settings.
Select “Post-alignment” in the option menu.
Set “Number of trials” to “5” and “Parameter step” to “1.0”.
Click on the “Start” button.
Scroll through 5 trial images.
Select the best image showing proper alignment with no doubling or blurring in the reconstructed image.
Ensure the software remembers the parameter value associated with the displayed image.
Verify that the preferred slice number and corresponding preview image are displayed on the screen before moving to the next step.
Select the "Start" tab in the "Reconstruction" window.
Click on "Fine tuning".
In the pop-up window, select "Ring-artifacts reduction".
Set “Number of trials” to “5”.
Set “Parameter step” to “1.0”.
Click "Start".
Repeat steps 14c–14e and select the lowest value that removes ring-artifacts.
Select the "Start" tab in the "Reconstruction" window again.
Click on "Fine tuning".
In the pop-up window, select "Smoothing".
Set “Number of trials” to “5”.
Set “Parameter step” to “1.0”.
Click "Start".
Repeat steps 14c–14e and choose the image/value that removes the most noise without overly blurring the image.
Select "Start" tab in the “Reconstruction” window.
Click on “Fine tuning”.
In the pop-up window, select “Beam hardening correction”.
Set “Number of trials” to “10” and “Parameter step” to “10”.
Click “Start”.
Repeat steps 14c–14e and select the best image.
Drag the left vertical line in the middle of the first peak in the histogram.
Drag the right vertical line just outside the right peak adjusting for voxel intensity.
Start Amira software.
Click on “Open Data” to open the reconstructed data files.
Enter the correct voxel size in x, y, and z (5 μm) when prompted.
Select all image files of the reconstructed data and click on “Open” button.
Initiate Watershed segmentation tool for automated object segmentation.
Seed materials by selecting voxels in a 2D section for myocardium and scar material.
Assign selected voxels to myocardium (red) and scar material (blue) using Amira software.
Manually curate minor inaccuracies in the segmentation process.
Review assigned voxels across ventricles in both 2D and 3D modes.
Enter the correct voxel size for volumetric measurements.
Open the "Segmentation" workroom by clicking on the "Segmentation" tab.
Create a new "Label field" in the Segmentation editor.
Optional: rename the "Label Field" (e.g., Heart_Segmentation) by clicking on the “Rename” button.
Click on the “Add” button to create 2 new materials in the “Materials” panel.
Rename one material as “Myocardium” and tick the boxes next to “2D” and “3D” options.
Rename another material as “Scar” and tick the boxes next to “2D” and “3D” options.
Click on the brush icon in the “Selection” panel.
Adjust the brush size with the size slider, as required.
Use the mouse pointer to mark the myocardial area in the 2D (XY) view mode.
Select the “Myocardium” material in the “Materials” panel.
Add the selected voxel by clicking the “+” button in the “Selection” panel.
Mark the scar area in the same slice and add selected voxels to “Scar” material.
Slide through different slices (2D mode) using a slider.
Select voxels throughout the heart and add selected voxels to the respective material as mentioned above.
Visualize all selected voxels in the chosen “Material” in 2D and 3D mode.
Select voxels with a brush for "Myocardium" material.
Avoid selecting voxels in “unintended” regions while adding to “Myocardium” material.
Proceed with segmentation using the Watershed tool after satisfying with selected voxels.
Click on the “Watershed” icon in the “Selection” panel.
Open the “Watershed” panel and click on the “Create new gradient image” button.
Click on “Apply and create a new label field” button to start the algorithm run.
Wait for the progress bar to indicate completion of the Watershed algorithm run.
Automated segmentation of scar and myocardium will be displayed in 2D/3D mode.
Slide through all slices in the 2D/3D view of the segmented heart.
If segmentation is mostly satisfactory, correct minor errors manually.
If seeding of materials is inadequate, toggle back to the “Label Field” file.
Seed additional voxels for proper material differentiation in 2D views (YZ and XZ).
Run the Watershed algorithm again after additional seeding.
Examine all slices in the 2D view for non-specific inclusion/exclusion of voxels.
Click the brush icon in the “Selection” panel.
Adjust the brush size with the slider.
Mark non-specific voxels in the 2D (XY) view mode.
Select the material to which the voxels belong.
Click the “+” button to add selected voxels to the intended material.
Click the “-” button to subtract selected voxels from the intended material.
Track and visualize the assigned or omitted voxels in 2D/3D mode.
Select “Segmentation” > “Material statistics” in the main menu once all corrections are made.
A table listing the volume of each material appears in a dialog box.
